contexts.text: The correspondence with man's external sensories: namely, with the sensory of sight, etc.

The eye communicates with the understanding more immediately than the rest of the sensory organs... Hence sight penetrates to the internal sensory which is in the brain by a shorter and more interior way. Explained.
The ear... receives speech, and bears it to the common sensory...
Correspond to those Societies... which have the greatest life and happiness, such as are those to which correspond the external and the internal sensories.
It is the internal sense which... disposes the external sensory... and therefore the sensories... accommodate themselves in a moment. (Continued. See Sense (bodily).)
All things sensated through the sensory organs inflow from internal things.
These delights are in these sensories from the influx of Heaven, where all the delight is of the use, and according to it.
[155a]. Wives are the sensories (of these deliciousnesses).
The sensories are quite dead without interior things.
The body with all its sensories is only an instrument...
It is the like with the internal sensories, which are of thought and affection...
The whole face, where are the sensories of sight, etc., corresponds to...
The sensories of the body are only recipients and percipients as of themselves. Enumerated. These five sensories sensate by influx from within, the things which inflow from without...
This may be illustrated by the sensories of man.
In the brains are the beginnings of the fibres, through which their forces... present in the sensories of the senses... DWis 2. 3.
